annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 414 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. During this Age of Men phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 414 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr

annotations.annotation_text: The Bug Fable opening (414.14): Shaun narrates a retelling of Aesop's fable 'The Ant and the Grasshopper'. The Ondt represents Shaun (industrious, thrifty, bourgeois) while the Gracehoper represents Shem/Joyce (artistic, prodigal, starving).
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
FinnegansWeb: The Ondt and the Gracehoper. https://www.finnegansweb.com

annotations.annotation_text: Polysyllabic thunderclap on page 414 ("Shaun the Post (First Watch)"): one of ten 100-letter words synthesizing thunder across world languages, signaling a Viconian cataclysm within Shaun floating down the Liffey in a barrel, delivering his sermon, the well-fed postman who delivers messages he cannot understand. This divine acoustic blast — fusing Hindi, Greek, Latin, French, Italian, Irish, and Norse roots — marks a civilizational transition in the Age of Men phase.
sources: Vico, Giambattista. Scienza Nuova (On the Thunder). https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/vico/
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Etymology of "The Ondt" (414.20): Danish 'ond' (evil, cruel) + Swedish 'ont' (pain) + German 'ohne' (without). Represents joyless puritanical capitalism and authoritarian conformity.
sources: Contemporary Literature Press: Scandinavian Languages. https://editura.mttlc.ro

annotations.annotation_text: Etymology of "The Gracehoper" (414.28): grasshopper + grace + hope. Joyce's autobiographical portrait of the destitute artist dancing, singing, and seeking theological grace rather than bank balances.
